judges.summary: I opened all five with my thumb resting at about y700 on a 390×844 screen, and the question I asked each was the same: without moving my hand or my eye, do I know which lamp, what it costs to deliver, when it comes, and how I get out? Threestep and window answer all four on the first screen with zero scrolls — threestep literally captions the questions (01 מה בחרת · 02 מה יעלה לקבל את זה · 03 תשלום) and prints all three approved terms with both halves, including דמי ביטול עד 5% או 100 ₪, at y394–514 with the 59px button at y637; window does the same with the ledger at y527–800 and puts its 56px button at y770, the most thumb-reachable control in the round. Slip has by far the best answer to leak 1 — שתי מנורות שביל סולאריות מנירוסטה, באור צהוב חם — לשביל. over the literal title, and the highest measured checkout dominance (2.19) — but I measured its 8–17 ימי עסקים row at y764, directly behind the pinned button, and the cancellation fee cap at y866, off screen: its terms=3/4 is a DOM count, and on the phone the shop tells me it is free to a pickup point and that I have 14 days, and says nothing about when the lamps arrive or what cancelling costs until I scroll. Meters has the only picture in the set that no other shop could use — the lit wire against the bare ground line, and תרומה למידה per line — but its opening block is the basket headline BRIEF §5.1 forbids, its two product-title links measure 34px, and at 320×568 the pay button falls 14px below the fold. Paydesk is the one I would not pay through: the drawer opens folded at 2 מנורות · 3 יחידות with two 38px thumbnails, so I cannot see that צהוב חם is in the basket at all without a tap, that tap makes the terms vanish, and its pay button sits at y189 — the far top of the phone, the one place my thumb cannot reach. Counting taps: one to pay in slip, meters, threestep and window; three in paydesk (unfold to check the variant, re-fold to re-read the cancellation clause, then pay), and every one of the five puts a ≥52px pill under the thumb except paydesk, which puts it under the eyebrow. I would pay through threestep and window without hesitating, through meters after squinting past the headline, and through slip only after one scroll to find out when it arrives — which is precisely the scroll this round was convened to remove.

judges.lens: Creative director who rejected round 1 as "from the nineties, everything repeated" — judging the 324px column as a typographic problem before a layout problem, from the renders first: does the still contain an idea only a lighting store could have, does the drawer separate from the night page behind it, does it belong to the same store as the finished product and collection pages, and is the empty state a composition or a placeholder.

scores.best: The only drawer that solves 324px as TYPE. Three voices in one column — an authored serif sentence with the chosen variant lit in glow ("שתי מנורות שביל סולאריות מנירוסטה, באור צהוב חם — לשביל."), the literal record beneath it in Heebo 300, and the line total in FRL glow. scores.worst: In the drawer only TWO terms are pinned: 8–17 ימי עסקים and the cancellation fee cap «עד 5% או 100 ₪» both live inside the נ.ב. INSIDE the scroll body (drawer.html:243–249), so the answer to "when does it come" is scroll-gated on the primary surface. judges.summary: Judged from the stills, only two of these five treat 324px as a typographic problem, and slip is the one that wins it: its drawer is the only column with three distinct voices — an authored serif sentence with the chosen variant lit in glow («…באור צהוב חם — לשביל.»), the literal product record beneath it in Heebo 300, and the line total in Frank Ruhl Libre — where every other concept sets a 14px sans title over a stepper and calls it hierarchy. That earns it dom=2.19/2.00/1.75/2.67, under44=0 on both files at all four viewports, and a desktop cart page (checkout t426, all four numbers in a hairline ledger in the SAME column as the button) that plainly belongs to the store that shipped the collection and product pages. window is the one that answers my second question: on shot-desktop the page behind is genuinely darkened and the panel is a lifted, lit surface with each line a plate and the subtotal on a haloed sill — the drawer separates because it is lit, not because it is outlined, which is the only argument this store should be making; it also measures exits=0, the only concept that stops offering a decided buyer a way back out. meters has the best single image in the round — a rail where twenty bulbs hang countable on a lit wire and two path lights stand on a bare ground line because they have no length — but it hangs that image on the basket headline BRIEF §5.1 rules out in terms, and the brief tells me to score what is left when the headline goes: a bordered stepper, an icon bin, a 34px title tap target, and a drawer checkout 14px below the fold at 320×568. threestep answers leaks 2 and 3 better than anyone (all three terms with subs above the button, cancellation last) and reasons more honestly than anyone, but its 01/02/03 bands are a funnel cliché that would paste into a shoe shop, its desktop panel is still a black panel on a black page, and its cart page carries 23 controls under 44px against a baseline of 25. paydesk is the boldest structural bet and the most robust file — checkout at y189 in every viewport, no JS needed for the fold — but it folds away the one thing the brief says the drawer owes first, and its CSS hides the terms whenever the proof list is open, so the cancellation clause vanishes at exactly the moment a buyer opens the list to check. Two visible defects deserve naming because both sit at the spot their NOTE claims to have fixed: window prints «89.90 ₪ ליחידה» directly under «89.90 ₪» on the quantity-1 line, and slip's honesty sentence is clipped mid-line by the scroll mask at the fold. Build slip, graft window's scrim and lit-sill hierarchy and threestep's three-row pinned ledger into it so no term is ever a scroll away, take meters' per-line «תרומה למידה» without its headline, and replace slip's dead minus/plus submits with paydesk's `/cart/change` links.

scores.best: The double-writing of every line — an authored Hebrew sentence in Frank Ruhl Libre ("שתי מנורות שביל סולאריות מנירוסטה, באור צהוב חם — לשביל.") with the literal product.title + variant.title in Heebo 300 directly beneath it, never truncated. In the mobile drawer shot the buyer reads their own decision and can still audit it; quantity spelled in words means a wrong count is caught by reading, not by counting. Nothing else in the set answers leak 1 twice over.
scores.worst: On the primary surface the cancellation FEE CAP is behind a scroll. The pinned pair above checkout carries only "0 ₪ … עד הבית 29.90 ₪." and the 14-day headline; "דמי ביטול עד 5% או 100 ₪ — הנמוך מביניהם." and the whole 8–17 row live in the נ.ב., which in the 390 render is a heading with its rows below the fold. Leak 3's expensive half is therefore not what is read before pressing.
violations: cart.html steppers are <button type="submit" name="minus"/"plus"> — Shopify's POST /cart honours only updates[], so without JS both controls submit and change nothing (a silent no-op). The separate "עדכון הפתק אחרי שינוי כמות" submit does satisfy INVENTORY-DRAWER's no-JS requirement, but the ± are dead where the other four concepts use /cart/change links.
Designer's own admission: at 320×568 the note scrolls before the second line is fully visible.

scores.best: The 288–343px hole is not shrunk, it is occupied by the answer: in the mobile drawer the terms ledger sits exactly where the void was, with the cancellation fee cap as the last thing above the button. And the cart page's ledger is introduced by "ארבעה מספרים, ואין חמישי." — the refusal to invent a fifth term printed on the page as a design element. Strongest honesty writing in the set.
scores.worst: The concept's load-bearing device is the one that degrades worst. judges.summary: Nothing in the five carries a banned device: I found no free-shipping progress bar, no threshold, no countdown or urgency copy, no badge, strikethrough or -N% (the only "-6%/-8%/-10%" strings in the files are radial-gradient positions), no stars, no review counts, no "trusted by", no WhatsApp, no fifth term, and no image from the WINNING-SPEC §3.6 never-use list — all five are zero-JS, radius-0 except pills, and carry the approved sentences verbatim once tag joins are normalised. The one substantive rule breach is meters: BRIEF §5.1 says the derived light-measure "may be used per line … and never as a basket headline", and meters opens both the drawer and the cart page with «5 מטר · 20 נורות · 2 מנורות» as exactly that headline, never engaging the ruling — its own note concedes a basket of three wall lights would print «3 מנורות» over a bare wire. A second, smaller breach is threestep's drawer empty state, which rewrites approved term 3 down to "14 יום לביטול מקבלת המוצר." and drops "לפי חוק הגנת הצרכן". slip wins on the two heaviest criteria: shot-mobile-1 shows every line written twice — the serif sentence with the chosen variant lit in glow, the untruncated product.title + variant.title beneath it — so the display face carries authored prose and never a product title, and shot-cart-desktop shows all four numbers with both subs as a hairline two-column ledger sitting in the same column as the checkout button, under an ElmsNest wordmark that makes it unmistakably the same store as the homepage and PDP. Its defects are real but reparable: the cancellation fee cap and the 8–17 row sit in the נ.ב. below the fold in the drawer render, and the cart-page ± are type=submit name="minus"/"plus", which POST /cart ignores — dead controls without JS where the other four use /cart/change links. window is the closest rival and the most honest document of the five ("ארבעה מספרים, ואין חמישי" over the ledger, plus an explicit refusal to print a final shipping number), but it leans its whole idea on backdrop-filter whose stated fallback is the very fixed-alpha dim the inventory called invisible on a black page, its line plates read as cards against "hairlines not boxes", and shot-cart-desktop carries an unfinished black rectangle under the summary sill. paydesk answers leaks 2 and 3 better than anyone — terms with both subs directly under the button, 4/4 on the cart page, the richest empty state — but its default drawer shows no product name at all, and opening the list to get that proof hides the terms, so it fails the leak the brief calls the drawer's first duty; threestep answers all three but its 01/02/03 bands and wordmark-less header are precisely the drawer a competitor could paste into a shoe shop.

judges.summary: Judged on whether a decided buyer gets paid, four of the five already win the round outright against the baseline — every one puts a 52–58px glow pill inside the phone fold on both surfaces against a y932 cart-page baseline, and every one kills the twin-button defect — so the ranking turns on attention cost and on invitations to leave. slip wins because its drawer fold at 390×844 is the only screen that lets a buyer verify their choice by reading rather than auditing ('שתי מנורות שביל סולאריות מנירוסטה, באור צהוב חם' with the count spelled in words), it pins 0 ₪ and 14 יום between the basket and the button so checkout cannot be reached without passing them, and it posts the round's highest dominance (2.19/2.00/1.75/2.67) with the only rival demoted to an underlined text link. meters is a close second and the most honest page in the round, but it spends the first ~400px of the drawer on a rail, two captions and a three-line disclaimer that answer none of the three questions, its title anchors are 34px exits, and its cart document runs to 4393px. threestep is the leanest composition and the only concept whose terms ledger is structurally guaranteed to be read before the button on both surfaces (y386→540 above a y641 checkout in the drawer; y392→520 above t578 on the cart) — but its cart checkout falls 81px below the fold at 320×568, its product titles become 36–38px exits, a full site footer adds a dozen more, and its one rival control is captioned 'ולבדוק שוב', which tells the buyer to doubt in the last line before paying. window has the best scrim in the round — its desktop shot is the only one where the page behind genuinely recedes — but the render shows '89.90 ₪' stacked over '89.90 ₪ ליחידה' on the qty-1 line, the same number twice, and its cart page hides all four terms behind a 'מה שכדאי לדעת' link while placing 'להמשך בחירה' above the button, so reassurance lands after the decision and an exit lands before it. paydesk has the strongest geometry of all (checkout at y308 at every phone width, dominance 1.82) and the weakest job: it folds away the proof that the right variant is in the basket, and the CSS that hides the terms when that fold is opened means proof and reassurance are never on screen together — then its cart page offers 'להוסיף עוד מנורה', a cross-sell, in the one place the brief says no new argument may start. Build slip, graft threestep's terms-above-button ordering onto its cart page, replace its JS-only steppers with meters' /cart/change links, and delete 'להמשיך להסתכל' from the fold.

The state a buyer lands in after add-to-cart shows no product name at all — only «2 מנורות · 3 יחידות» and two 38px thumbnails — when the brief's first demand is proof that the right lamp is in the basket. Worse, shot-mobile-2 shows that opening the proof removes the terms: .desk:has(+ .basket[open]) .terms drops the ledger to 0/4 in exactly the state where the buyer is checking carefully. The two leaks are never plugged at the same moment.

terms hidden whenever the basket is open (terms=3/4 folded, 0/4 unfolded)
cart.html has no input[name="updates[]"] anywhere — a contract element dropped and no typed-quantity path

grafts.device: The two-voice line: an authored serif sentence with the chosen variant lit in glow, and directly beneath it the literal product.title + variant.title in Heebo 300 with overflow-wrap:anywhere, never truncated.
grafts.why: It is the only construction that answers leak 1 twice, and the second voice is what makes the first safe to build: if the Liquid sentence falls to its generic branch, the record line still carries the exact title and variant. Build the sentence as a template — gendered numeral word from a 1–10 table (else «{{ n }} יחידות»), a plural noun per product.type (≈8 authored strings), the variant title, and the place kicker the card already computes — and never let it be the only place a title appears.

grafts.device: At quantity 1 the minus is an inert <span>, not a link and not a button; remove is a single word (הסרה) elsewhere on the row.
grafts.why: window, paydesk and meters all point the qty-1 minus at /cart/change?quantity=0, which reinstates the baseline's two-identical-deletes defect as two links and lets a no-JS mis-tap delete a line. An inert span is the only version where removes=[1,1] is true with scripting off. meters' disabled attribute on the drawer's <button name="minus"> is the same fix for the JS surface.

grafts.device: The complete no-JS cart stepper: − · · +, plus a visible
grafts.why: It is the only one of the five that satisfies all three of INVENTORY's no-JS requirements at once — change a quantity, stay on the page, and keep updates[] for Kalles' JS to enhance in place. slip's submit-button steppers are inert without JS; threestep and window have the links but no update submit; paydesk dropped updates[] entirely. This is the shape main-cart.liquid ships.

grafts.device: The surface: a scrim that is alpha plus a backdrop brightness reduction with an @supports not (backdrop-filter) block that raises opacity; a panel genuinely lighter than the page; and the terms ledger as the flex-grower with space-evenly.
grafts.why: The desktop renders settle it — window's page behind is visibly dimmed while slip's and meters' are fully legible, which is finding #1 of the inventory actually fixed rather than restated. Making the ledger the grower is also the structural cure for the 288–343px void: on a 1-line basket the slack becomes air between hairlines, and on an 8-line basket the ledger compresses before the button does.

grafts.device: Suppress the per-unit row when quantity == 1: print the line total alone, and «169.90 ₪ ליחידה» only where 1 × price and the total differ.
grafts.why: window and paydesk both render «89.90 ₪» above «89.90 ₪ ליחידה» on the garland line — the same number printed twice on the narrowest surface in the store. One {%- if item.quantity > 1 -%} removes it, and the rule generalises: never print an arithmetic step that cannot differ from its result.

grafts.device: Empty state: the lit window-mullion glyph with «האור כבר דולק. חסר רק המקום.», over slip's four-place hairline ledger (שביל · קיר · גינה · מרפסת, each with the place it lights, rows ≥56px, flexed to fill) and one pill «לקטלוג — 27 מנורות».
grafts.why: Together they are the two halves the brief asks for — an invitation, not an error screen, in the store's own vocabulary — and they replace the stock Kalles grey cart-with-an-✕ with a drawing only a lighting shop can use. meters' and paydesk's numbered place lists and meters' «0 מטר · 0 נורות» are the versions to leave behind.

judges.summary: Judged from the renders, slip (8.40) and window (8.35) are a photo finish and the build should be slip's composition on window's surface. slip's shot-mobile-1 is the only image in the round where the thing the buyer chose two clicks ago is the largest coloured object on the line — «באור צהוב חם» in glow inside a 19px serif sentence, with the full product.title and variant.title unclipped in Heebo directly beneath — which kills the ellipsis and the grey-13px-variant defects simultaneously, and its cart page puts subtotal and button at t370 with the four-number ledger in the same column as the button instead of three boxes below it. window's desktop shot proves the one claim nobody else can: the catalogue behind is genuinely dimmed and blurred, while slip's and meters' desktop renders leave the page behind fully legible — inventory finding #1 fixed rather than described. On the derived-number question the answer is settled and costs no metafield: DERIVED-DATA gives working Liquid that pulls metres and bulbs out of variant.title with split on 'מ׳'/'נורות' while excluding the '×' area case, but only per line — meters puts «5 מטר · 20 נורות · 2 מנורות» at the head of the drawer and the head of the cart page, which is the one thing §5.1 forbids, and scored on what remains it drops to fourth. The no-JS ranking inverts the aesthetic one: meters is the only cart page carrying links plus updates[] plus a visible עדכון submit, threestep is the only one whose qty-1 minus cannot delete a line (window, paydesk and meters all point it at quantity=0 beside a הסרה to the same URL, reinstating the baseline's twin-bin defect), and slip is the weakest — its ± are type=submit name="minus", inert with scripting off, so it must adopt meters' link stepper verbatim. paydesk (6.15) is last on the criterion that carries 35 points: shot-mobile-1 shows a drawer that names no product at all by default, and shot-mobile-2 shows the terms ledger disappearing the moment the basket is opened, so leak 1 and leaks 2–3 are never answered in the same state — though its <details> fold is the right emergency device for an 8-line basket, where slip's two-voice lines are the most verbose in the set and window's ledger is the first thing squeezed. Stress cases the mockups all dodge: a 30-variant title («1.5×1.5 מ׳ / 96 LED / צהוב») has no prose form, so slip's sentence must degrade to a template whose failure mode is a flat label rather than broken Hebrew; a 1-item basket makes threestep's fixed 154px band 02 and meters' rail apparatus disproportionate while window's space-evenly ledger absorbs it; and not one of the five renders item.error_message, even though the inventory measured it at 11.86:1 and handed the treatment to the rebuild — the winner owes it a hairline row inside the line, not a red band. Finally, much less of this is new CSS than it looks: elmsnest-v2-core.liquid already ships the sky/gold/glow/hair/scrim tokens, .env2-btn (the glow pill, 44px on mobile), .env2-btn--ghost, .env2-link with its ::before touch inflation, .env2-hair, .env2-eyebrow, .env2-h, .env2-serif and .env2-price, and elmsnest-v2-coll-terms.liquid already ships the numeral+unit+headline+sub hairline ledger every concept prints — so the genuinely new work in the two sections is the panel surface, the line-item grid, the /cart/change stepper, and slip's sentence.

designs.idea: The basket is measured in light rather than in SKUs: the drawer opens with one derived, checkable line — «5 מטר · 20 נורות · 2 מנורות» — drawn as a rail where bulbs hang on a lit wire because they have a length and lamps stand on a bare ground line because they do not, and every item prints the share it contributed.
designs.weakest: The measure is only as interesting as the basket: this one has a single measurable line, so the rail carries one lit span and two standing marks — a basket of three wall lights would print «3 מנורות» over a bare wire, which is honest but visually thin, and on a one-item basket the top block is a lot of apparatus for one number. I refused to pad it (no invented scale, no "typical garden" reference), so on the smallest baskets the drawer's opening block has to earn its space with type alone.

designs.idea: The cart is not a table of rows but a short note the shop writes back to you — a Hebrew sentence in Frank Ruhl Libre saying what you just chose ("שתי מנורות שביל סולאריות מנירוסטה, באור צהוב חם — לשביל.") with the numbers under it as a quiet ledger, so the buyer recognises their own decision instead of auditing a spreadsheet; the cart page is the same note, longer, on headed paper.
designs.weakest: The sentence must be written by Liquid, and Liquid does not conjugate Hebrew: "שתי מנורות שביל" needs a gendered numeral and a plural agreeing with product.type, "גרילנדה אחת" the feminine — roughly 40 lines of case/when over ~8 product types plus a numeral table for 1–10 with a "{{n}} יחידות" fallback, and a wrong branch produces broken Hebrew rather than a merely awkward label, which a generic table can never do. Mitigated in the markup (the record line always carries the literal title and variant, and the sign-off falls back to cart.item_count, which needs no grammar) but it is the real cost of the idea. Secondary: at 320×568 the note scrolls before the second line is fully visible — below the brief's 324px floor, but real on an old phone.
